messages:
elaine: hey folks — opening a tiny PR to replace the long 429 runbook sample with a compact "rescue" script + SDK examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6789

ryan: lgtm. can you include both curl and node/go snippets? a lot of customers look for quick copy/paste.

maria: +1 on multi-lang. also, can we make the sample show graceful fallback to smaller model + retry header? that's what ops usually recommends.

elaine: yeah plan is: curl (short), node (fetch style), go (http.Client). fallback logic will be pseudocode with explicit backoff jitter. sample filename: docs/runbooks/429-rescue-compact.md

kevin: small nit — don't call out specific token counts in examples. reference the generic ctx_length param instead. also add a link to the context trimming helper: https://internal.redwood.dev/context-clipper

ryan: i'll review code snippets. also suggest adding a test harness snippet users can copy to validate 429s locally (uses --simulate-429 env flag)

elaine: upload in a followup commit. snippet for jittered backoff:

```
wait = base * (1 + rand())
for i in range(retries):
  sleep(wait)
  wait *= 2
```

maria: include explicit fallback order: 1) trim prompt 2) prefer cached KV prefix 3) switch to quantized model variant 4) last-resort smaller model. short bullet list works.

docs-bot: reminder — rename any existing anchors that point to old runbook: /runbooks/429-fallback -> /runbooks/429-rescue-compact (automated redirect will be set up but link sweep recommended)

kevin: i'll take anchor sweep. elaine, if you can add a one-line compatibility table for SDK versions (node >= 18, go >= 1.20) that'd be perfect.

elaine: will do. aiming to merge by EOD. tagging @ryan @maria for final approvals :thumbsup:

ryan: approving once go snippet uses http.NewRequestWithContext

maria: approved from docs side, thanks!

elaine: merged — thanks all. follow-up issue created for telemetry example tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1234
